decisions.reason: As a flagship cloud transactional email service, it sits squarely in the firm's core messaging knowledge base and strategic move toward multichannel cloud communication, so management would likely keep refining rather than withdraw it.

Document capture and recognition is adjacent to the firm's document workflow and integration capabilities, and the cited customer adoption suggests the firm has enough related knowledge and market feedback to continue developing it.

Email and fax conversion directly leverages the firm's established expertise in secure multichannel messaging for regulated processes, making it a product the firm is well positioned to sustain despite some legacy-technology risk.

Fax delivery optimization is narrowly scoped and exposed to longer-term fax decline, but it still fits the firm's installed base, technical know-how, and German demand for reliable compliant communications, so management would more likely keep than drop it in the next year.

Email sandbox threat protection complements the firm's security-led messaging offer and benefits from its R&D and operational expertise, so it is likely to remain part of the portfolio as a value-adding security service.
